text:
ashley: ran a focused nsys capture on the 8k -> 2k seqlen switch that triggers the perf regression. attaching quick notes.

kai: can you paste the exact command you used to reproduce?

ashley: \u003e repro loop: ./tools/run_infer.sh --model rwv2-small --batch 16 --max-seqlen 8192 --request-seqlen 2048 --trace nsys --out /tmp/trace

phil: saw this locally too. kernel selection falls back to the generic fp32-gemm path when seqlen drops, which ends up being slower than the optimized fp16 kernels for this model.

luis: that fallback should only happen if the autotuner marks the optimized kernel incompatible. maybe the stride calc is off for short prefix reuse?

ashley: attached the nsys timeline snapshot (see link in thread). main hotspot is a 50ms spike in matmul::fallback after KV cache warms up. prefix cache hit rate drops from ~92% to ~68% around the same time.

perf-bot: quick stats: p50 latency +18%, p95 +34% on 2k seqlen window. cpu overhead for dispatcher +7%.

kai: do we have perfetto traces for the same run? nsys is good for kernels but I want to correlate user threads and scheduling.

ashley: added perfetto by running with --trace perfetto. uploaded both traces to the run folder: s3://redwood-traces/1968001234/{nsys,perfetto}.

phil: looking at the perfetto CPU lane: there's a brief GC-like stall in the prefix cache housekeeping task (cache_rewrite_worker). it holds a lock for ~12ms and blocks dispatcher threads.

luis: aha. cache_rewrite_worker appears to flush partially invalidated prefixes when the reuse counter crosses threshold. on the short seqlen window the reuse counter hits an edge-case and triggers extra work.

ashley: stack snippet from nsys (kernel side):
```
gpu: matmul_opt_v2
gpu: matmul_generic_fp32 <-- heavy
gpu: kv_read
gpu: kv_write
```

kai: plan: 1) reproduce with smaller unit test that toggles reuse counter, 2) add telemetry to cache_rewrite_worker to log reason for flush, 3) try forcing kernel selection flag to prefer fp16 path to confirm speedup.

phil: I can add a runtime guard so fallback only happens if the autotuner returns "incompatible" explicitly. that should avoid accidental fallthroughs.

luis: quick mitigation idea: when prefix hit rate > 80% keep reuse_counter hysteresis longer (i.e., only decrement after N misses) so transient seqlen changes don't trigger flush. low risk config toggle.

ashley: applied a patch to dev branch that increases hysteresis (PR: https://git.redwood/infra/pull/4821). running regression tests now.

perf-bot: benchmark run queued. estimated 45m. will post results here.

devops-bot: rolled a canary with patched runtime to canary pool rwinf-canary-3. will route 5% traffic.

kai: if canary looks good, we should try toggling kernel_select_force_fp16 for that canary to validate kernel hypothesis.

ashley: manual forced run with kernel_select_force_fp16=1 shows p95 back down to baseline and matmul_generic_fp32 disappears from timeline.

phil: good sign. but we need to ensure numeric parity for callers — add unit test for fp16 path outputs within tolerance.

luis: I'll add cache_rewrite telemetry and a short lived metric: cache_flush_reason tagged by prefix_len_range + reuse_delta. want to capture distribution over next 24h.

ashley: perf-bot finished: hysteresis patch -> p95 -9%, p50 -3%, prefix hit rate +6%. canary metrics look stable over 1h. posting graphs in thread.

kai: next steps: 1) merge hysteresis patch, 2) add autotuner strictness check to avoid silent fallbacks, 3) follow-up run to evaluate long-tail workloads (variable seqlen mixes).

phil: will open PR for autotuner guard. tagging @luis for telemetry changes.

luis: ack. I'll keep an eye on the new metric and notify if flush_reason spikes.

ashley: summary: root cause appears to be an interaction between reuse_counter hysteresis and kernel selection fallthrough that together cause extra cache churn and an unintended generic-gemm fallback. mitigations landed in canary and look promising.

kai: nice work. can we add a short blurb to the runtime changelog so SREs know this change affects KV cache heuristics?

ashley: will draft changelog note after merges.

phil: reminder: keep the perf traces for 7 days in the trace bucket; they'll be useful if any regressions pop up post-merge.

perf-bot: archival scheduled: traces retained until 7 days after thread_ts.

ashley: thanks all :thumbsup:
